L11: 
L12: By Depop
L13: 
L14: 20 Dec 2025
L15: New York, NY - December 19, 2025 Depop, the global peer-to-peer fashion marketplace, has released its cite8†2026 Trends Report†downloads.ctfassets.net , The Edited Self, revealing a decisive cultural shift in how fashion consumers express identity, navigate choice and participate in culture.
L16: Building on last year’s insight into cite9†The New Fundamentals , this year's report uncovers how global pressures, digital saturation and an accelerated trend cycle have prompted a move toward sharper, more intentional personal style.
L17: Across the Depop community, people are choosing clarity over clutter. They are repeating silhouettes, refining core staples and curating wardrobes that reflect lived-in authenticity rather than fast-moving microtrends. At the same time, major global moments in 2026, including the World Cup and the U.S. 250th, draw people back into public life and shape new reasons to gather, dress with presence and signal belonging.
L18: Rooted in proprietary Depop insights, platform search and sales data and cultural research, The Edited Self outlines four key trends defining how style will evolve in the year ahead, focusing on the following four defining trends.
L19: Modern Uniforms: Consistency Becomes the New Flex.
L20: In an environment shaped by decision fatigue, economic tension and constant digital noise, people are gravitating toward dependable silhouettes and repeatable staples. Neutral palettes, sharp tailoring, boxy knits and crisp button-downs anchor wardrobes with ease. Across Depop, search interest reflects this shift, with spikes in workwear jackets, peacoats and office shirts. Modern Uniforms is about dressing with conviction and signaling taste through repetition rather than reinvention.
L21: Neo Nostalgia: Editing the Past to Soften the Present
L22: As uncertainty continues to influence emotional and aesthetic choices, nostalgia becomes a grounding mechanism. Rather than recreating a single era, Gen Z and young Millennials are blending fragments of the 70s, 90s and early 2000s to form a visual language that feels familiar and personal. Era mixing, archival pieces and expressive layering drive this trend, with Depop searches for bandage dresses, JNCO jorts and medieval-inspired silhouettes rising significantly.
L23: Everyday Ceremony: Bringing Intentionality to Daily Routines
L24: People are dressing with more purpose. Everyday activities become opportunities for small rituals and self-expression, with tailored coats, draped skirts, metallic fabrics and bold accessories elevating even the simplest routines. Search behavior on Depop shows strong gains across structured blazers, kitten heels and statement jewelry. Confidence and emotional comfort fuel this trend, with users dressing up as a way to feel more present in their day-to-day lives.
L25: 
L26: Romanticized Sports: Elegance Meets Ease
L27: Sportswear continues to evolve beyond performance into a new form of playful, soft-edged athleticism. Tennis whites, vintage jerseys, bike shorts and ski layers are styled with silk, tailoring and ballet flats to create looks that balance comfort with aspiration. In a World Cup year, athletic references take on added cultural meaning.
L28: Depop data shows major spikes in interest for vintage Lululemon, upcycled jerseys and ski-inspired pieces, signaling a continued appetite for reworked and elevated sports staples.
L29: A New Cultural Reset:
L30: 
L31: 2026 marks a moment of collective recalibration. Consumers are choosing quality over quantity, emotional connection over novelty and personal authorship over algorithm-driven churn. Across all four trends, a consistent narrative emerges. People want to feel grounded. They want clothes that reflect who they are. They want wardrobes shaped by confidence, comfort and individuality.

L35: About Depop
L36: Depop is the community-powered circular fashion marketplace where anyone can buy, sell and discover desirable, affordable secondhand fashion. Together with its community of approximately 43.5 million registered users, Depop is on a mission to make fashion circular - encouraging more people to choose secondhand and extend the lives of their clothes, redefining fashion consumption. Founded in 2011, Depop is headquartered in London, with an office in New York, and has a team of approximately 400 employees.
L37: In 2021, Depop became a wholly-owned subsidiary of Etsy - the global marketplace for unique and creative goods - and continues to operate as a standalone company. Find out more at www.depop.com.

L77: # How to Pack a Cabin Bag for a 5-Day Trip (with Checklist)
L78: 
L79: By Divya DoshiAugust 18, 2026
L80: 
L81:  A 5-day trip fits comfortably in a cabin bag if you pack around 5–6 tops, 2–3 bottoms, one layering piece, underwear and socks for the trip length, and one pair of extra shoes — all built around a single color palette so pieces mix and match. Roll clothes instead of folding, and use the "one bag, one plan" rule: decide your outfits before you pack, not while you're packing.
L82: Here's a complete system, plus a checklist you can run through before you zip up.
L83: ## The core packing list for 5 days
L84: 
L85: Category  | Quantity
L86: Tops  | 5–6
L87: Bottoms  | 2–3
L88: Layering piece (jacket/cardigan)  | 1
L89: Underwear  | 5–6 pairs
L90: Socks  | 5–6 pairs
L91: Sleepwear  | 1 set
L92: Shoes (in addition to worn pair)  | 1 pair
L93: Toiletry kit  | 1 (travel-sized, under 100ml per item)
L94: Chargers & electronics  | As needed
L95: This list assumes a mixed-use trip — work or leisure, moderate climate. Adjust up for cold-weather trips (add a warmer layer, swap in bulkier footwear) or down for beach trips (fewer layers, more swimwear).
L96: ## Step-by-step packing method
L97: 
L98:   1. Lay out your outfits before you pack, not while packing. Pick a base color (navy, black, or beige works well) and build 5–6 outfit combinations from a smaller set of pieces that mix and match. This is the single biggest space-saver — packing "outfits" instead of random items always uses more room than packing a coordinated capsule.
L99:   2. Roll, don't fold, casual clothing. Rolled clothes take up less space than folded ones and reduce deep creases. Reserve folding for structured items like blazers or dress shirts that roll poorly.
L100: 
L101:   3. Use packing cubes to separate categories. One cube for tops, one for bottoms, one for underwear and socks keeps everything visible and prevents you from unpacking the entire bag to find one item. cite18†WNTR's packing cubes are built for exactly this.
L102:   4. Pack shoes in a separate bag or the outer pocket, soles facing outward, and stuff socks or small items inside them to use the wasted space.
L103: 
L104:   5. Keep liquids in a single transparent resealable bag, each container 100 ml or under, positioned near the top for quick access at security.
L105: 
L106:   6. Fill gaps with small items last — chargers, a travel adapter, and toiletry extras go into leftover corners rather than their own dedicated space.
L107:   7. Weigh your bag before you leave home. Most Indian cabin allowances cap at 7 kg — a kitchen or bathroom scale gives you an accurate reading before you're at the airport counter.
L108: ## What NOT to pack in cabin baggage
L109: 
L110: A few categories are worth leaving out of your cabin bag specifically, even if they're allowed in principle:
L111: 
L112:   * Liquids over 100 ml — these get confiscated at security regardless of value or intent; pack full-size bottles in checked baggage if you're bringing any.
L113: 
L114:   * Anything you're not prepared to lose access to mid-security-check — passports and documents are fine, but avoid burying anything you might need to quickly hand over or reference.
L115:   * Bulky souvenirs you're hoping to buy on the trip — if you're planning to shop, pack lighter than your cabin bag's full capacity on the way out, leaving room for the return.
L116: 
L117:   * A second full bag disguised as a "personal item" — airlines increasingly enforce the one-bag-plus-personal-item rule strictly; an overstuffed tote won't pass as a small personal item.
L118: ## Adjusting the list for your specific trip
L119: 
L120: The core list above assumes a moderate climate and mixed work/leisure use, but a few common trip types need small adjustments:
L121: 
L122:   * Business trip: Swap two casual tops for one extra formal shirt, add a compact toiletry bag with grooming essentials, and prioritize a laptop-compatible personal item over extra shoes.
L123:   * Beach or warm-weather trip: Reduce layering pieces to zero, add 2–3 swimwear items, and include a compact travel towel if your destination doesn't guarantee one.
L124: 
L125:   * Cold-weather trip: This is the hardest to fit in cabin-only — bulky sweaters and jackets eat space fast. Consider wearing your heaviest jacket onto the flight rather than packing it, which frees significant cabin space.
L126:   * Wedding or event trip: One formal outfit takes up disproportionate space compared to casual wear. If you're bringing an ethnic outfit like a saree or lehenga, pack it as the very top layer using the rolling technique in our cite19†saree and lehenga packing guide rather than folding it in with everyday clothes.
L127: ## The pre-departure checklist
L128: 
L129: Run through this the night before, not the morning of your flight:
L130: 
L131:   * Outfits planned and laid out before packing (not decided while packing)
L132: 
L133:   * Clothes rolled, not folded, where possible
L134: 
L135:   * Liquids under 100 ml each, in a single transparent resealable bag
L136: 
L137:   * Shoes packed soles-out with socks stuffed inside
L138: 
L139:   * Chargers, adapter, and cables packed together, not scattered
L140: 
L141:   * Bag weighed on a home scale — confirm it's under your airline's cabin limit
L142:   * Passport, boarding pass, and ID accessible without digging through the whole bag
L143: 
L144:   * Personal item packed separately from the main cabin bag, not stuffed inside it
